10.1002_advs.202522562: Cubic‐garnet‐type solid electrolytes (SEs) are promising candidates for all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) due to their high ionic conductivity and stability against lithium metal. However, intrinsic lithium and oxygen vacancies formed during high‐temperature sintering can lead to interfacial metal reduction and phase transitions, ultimately causing short circuits. In this study, we quantified these intrinsic vacancies in Li 6.5 La 3 Zr 1.5 Ta 0.5 O 12 (LLZTO) and proposed a strategy to achieve vacancy‐suppressed, lithium‐stuffed garnet SEs by simply tuning the lithium content in both the green pellet and bedding powder during sintering. The optimized Li‐stuffed LLZTO exhibited lithium occupancy exceeding 6.5 per formula unit (pfu) and oxygen‐vacancy concentrations below 0.02 pfu, resulting in improved chemical stability at the electrolyte–electrode interface and enhanced air stability. The garnet electrolyte demonstrated a critical current density of 1.00 mA cm −2 at 30°C and 1.75 mA cm −2 at 60°C, along with stable cycling performance over 3000 h in lithium symmetric cells and 2000 cycles in hybrid full‐cells, demonstrating 90% capacity retention. These findings highlight the pivotal role of intrinsic vacancy control in enhancing the structural and electrochemical integrity of garnet electrolytes, thereby promoting their practical application in ASSBs.
10.1002_advs.78441: Dissatisfactory electrochemical performance of wide‐temperature lithium‐sulfur batteries (LSBs) originates from the sluggish Li + desolvation and successive sulfur specie conversion kinetics at the interface and within the cathode interior. Herein, different from electrolyte engineering, a self‐tandem catalysis enabled cascade reactions is developed to drive Li + kinetics and associated polysulfide conversions in wide‐temperature LSBs. By incorporating electron‐adjustable atom‐level Ce as the self‐tandem catalyst onto defect‐rich Co, Fe‐based layered double hydroxides (EAAC@D‐LDH), a favorable solvation microenvironment is established to decrease the related barriers toward promoting rapid Li + desolvation, sulfur conversion, and Li 2 S delithiation kinetics, as revealed in Raman analysis, electrochemical evaluations, and ex‐situ interfacial morphology as well as composition characterization. Such improved reaction kinetics enable the sulfur cathodes work well in a wide temperature ranging from 0 to ‐30°C, and it retains high‐capacity retention of 94% at 5C. Under ‐20°C, the cells remain the capacity of 85% at 0.1C, respectively. Remarkably, a stable capacity is reserved even at an ultralow temperature of ‐30°C, demonstrating that the substantial promise of this self‐tandem catalysis supports cascade reaction refinement strategy toward high performance wide‐temperature LSBs.
10.1002_inf2.70194: Artificial synapses based on organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are promising candidates for neuromorphic computing, yet their performance is critically limited by non‐volatile state retention. Although polyelectrolytes offer a new approach, existing options fail due to extremely low ion migration rates. This limitation arises largely from the intrinsic kinetics of ion transport within the electrolyte. Here, a kinetic regulation strategy is demonstrated using a blended electrolyte composed of a poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) and an ionic liquid (IL). The high glass transition temperature ( T g ) of the PIL restricts segmental motion, creating a rigid matrix that effectively immobilizes the counter‐ions (cations). This kinetic trapping effect significantly suppresses their spontaneous diffusion into the semiconductor channel during the relaxation phase, thereby preventing the neutralization of TFSI − dopants and preserving the induced polarons for superior non‐volatile retention. Meanwhile, the small‐molecule IL acts as a plasticizer to ensure sufficient ion mobility for gate voltage response. Consequently, the optimized device (40 wt.% PIL) achieves superior performance, exhibiting a synaptic state retention of 31.71% after 30 s, a nearly fivefold enhancement over the pure ionic liquid control. This kinetic control also significantly reduces the nonlinearity ( NL ) value for long‐term potentiation by 49.3%. In artificial neural network simulations, the device achieves a high recognition accuracy of 90.1%. This work demonstrates that kinetic regulation is a robust strategy to optimize state retention while maintaining sufficient response characteristics. image
10.1016_j.apenergy.2026.128115: Protonic ceramic electrochemical cells are a promising technology for low-carbon energy and fuel production. The technology offers several benefits, including high efficiency, the absence of precious metals, and the potential to couple thermochemical and electrochemical processes within a single device. However, modelling defect transport in protonic ceramic membranes, which is crucial for optimizing device performance, presents significant challenges due to the complexity of the often-used Nernst-Planck-Poisson equations. This work introduces a new analytical solution for these equations, providing a direct and straightforward method for computing fluxes of multiple charged species and electric potential differences across the protonic ceramic membrane under steady-state conditions. The analytical solution shows excellent performance against more complex transient numerical solutions of the Nernst-Planck-Poisson equations available in literature. This computationally inexpensive approach offers valuable insights into membrane performance, including identifying conditions that minimize ohmic losses and maximize energy efficiency, and providing optimal membrane thicknesses that balance the counterproductive polaron fluxes and voltage drop across the membrane. Additionally, the proposed method enables quick but effective membrane material selection for various devices such as electrolysers, fuel cells, and proton pumping membranes for gas separation. In addition, semi-empirical relationships are utilized to extend the algebraic model’s capabilities for evaluating the full electrochemical cell (membrane + electrodes) in both electrolysis and fuel cell modes. The full cell algebraic model shows good agreement with experimental data on ceramic electrolysis cells. Finally, the supplementary material includes an Excel worksheet which implements the analytical model.
10.1021_acs.est.5c03324: Both legacy (e.g., polybrominated diphenyl ethers; PBDEs) and emerging (e.g., hexabromobenzene) flame retardants frequently feature brominated aromatic motifs, which are associated with persistent and bioaccumulative properties. While activated carbon has been used to treat brominated aromatics, it is a passive sorbent and does not degrade them. Using model bromobenzenes, this study illustrates debromination of brominated aromatics sorbed to activated carbon when the carbon is fashioned into cathodes and treated at a −1.3 V/SHE applied potential. Debromination rates fit a quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR), increasing with increasing free energy changes (Δ G ) for a two-electron transfer to the brominated aromatic. Half-lives ranged from ∼4 min for hexabromobenzene to ∼15 d for bromobenzene, although the debromination half-life for bromobenzene decreased to ∼50 h at −1.8 V/SHE. The QSAR for bromobenzene debromination was also predictive for debromination of two PBDEs (BDE-99 and BDE-47), indicating that the QSAR was broadly applicable across brominated aromatic structures. Debromination released bromide to the catholyte, while lower-order brominated aromatic intermediates remained sorbed to the cathode. Debromination rates roughly correlated with the conductivity of the black carbon. The strong sorption capacity of carbon-based cathodes permits sequestration of brominated aromatics from contaminated waters within short hydraulic residence times, while an electric potential can be periodically applied to debrominate contaminants sequestered on the carbon.
10.1021_acs.est.5c07500: Liquid alkaline water electrolysis (LAWE) is a demonstrated technology for hydrogen production, yet a comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA) of their deployment is lacking. Research leading to improvements to the core component, the electrochemical stack, along with auxiliary system materials and dynamic operation of stacks from variable electricity supply offers new data that allows for detailed modeling and evaluation. Here, we present an LCA of two facility designs based on the current state-of-the-art stack and an advanced stack with zero-gap between electrodes, and capture dynamic electricity use from solar, wind, and hybrid sources and stack recycling strategies. We present life cycle impact factors characterizing the production of 1 kg of hydrogen across 12 environmental, human health, and resource impact categories (TRACI and ReCiPe) in the contiguous United States. As expected, the source of electricity will drive impacts (e.g., 83–94% of carbon intensity); however, we find that operating using wind electricity can lower hydrogen leakage and the overall carbon intensity (1.03 kgCO2e/kgH2) relative to solar electricity (2.57 kgCO2e/kgH2) at matched 1:1 capacity between LAWE and the electricity source. The deployment of the advanced design and stack recycling lowers impacts across all life cycle stages. We highlight opportunities to further reduce potential impacts, including the balance of plant materials and operation cycles associated with the use of variable wind and solar electricity that result in hydrogen leakage.
10.1021_acs.est.6c01602: Conventional electrochemical water treatment typically focuses on anodic oxidation or cathodic reduction. In contrast, highly efficient anode–cathode synergy can achieve effects beyond the capability of either single electrode, enabling low-carbon and sustainable pollutant removal. Herein, we developed a reagent- and aeration-free system for continuous ·OH generation by integrating anodic O 2 evolution with cathodic H 2 O 2 production and activation cascades in a dual-cathode stacked flow-through electrochemical reactor. Low-cost graphite felt (GF) and stainless-steel mesh (SSM) cathodes selectively facilitated O 2 /H 2 O 2 and H 2 O 2 /·OH conversions. The stacked flow-through design established a self-sustaining ·OH production pathway, driving O 2 transport from the anode to the GF cathode for H 2 O 2 generation, followed by directional H 2 O 2 delivery to the SSM cathode for ·OH formation. Compared to a single-cathode system, the dual-cathode design maintained high Cr(VI) reduction (>95%) while enhancing Ni-EDTA decomplexation and total organic carbon (TOC) removal by up to 41% and 70%, respectively. Under optimized conditions (2.5 V, 2.5 mL/min), the dimensionally stable anode (DSA)/GF-SSM stacked flow-through system achieved 100% Cr(VI) detoxification, 99.9% Ni-EDTA decomplexation, and 50.8% TOC mineralization. Moreover, it demonstrated exceptional longevity and industrial scalability through continuous operation for 50 days. This study presents a feasible energy-efficient ·OH generation strategy, offering a practical, sustainable, and environmentally friendly solution for treating complex wastewater.
